2.content:
This Statement of Work covers Google Silicon COT Supply Chain, an implementation engagement to establish the data, planning, and system foundations required for Google’s direct operating model with TSMC and OSAT partners, including structured data exchange, lot-level traceability, and supply planning that treats yield uncertainty as a core planning input across E2Open, SAP S/4, and Kinaxis.

- Establish the implementation foundation for supplier visibility, ERP-backed traceability, and silicon supply planning across the target operating model.
- Enable unit-, lot-, and yield-related data flows from manufacturing partners into Google’s planning and execution landscape to support transparent cost, traceability, and replanning decisions.
- Deliver a phased rollout approach that supports wafer-level planning, key integration pathways, and future analytical capability expansion while preserving clear scope boundaries for Google-owned commercial decisions.

Deferred design decisions, scope assumptions, and unresolved dependencies are captured in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Google is expanding its Silicon COT supply chain capability across SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis in a landscape that requires a clearer AS-IS baseline before final design and execution. The current state includes foundry and OSAT purchase-order flows, material and supplier master setup, batch and lot traceability, subcontracting settlement, E2Open-based supply collaboration, and SAP enterprise-structure elements that must support the Silicon business model.

The engagement is driven by a need to define a scalable target state for silicon planning and execution as business complexity, data volume, and scenario-based planning increase. Google must confirm how silicon planning should operate across Kinaxis and adjacent systems, including data-ingestion points, boundary systems, integration flows, and the extent to which the existing Kinaxis instance can absorb additional silicon scope without affecting current operations.

Key pain points include incomplete visibility into current process and data gaps, unclear readiness of the existing application and infrastructure footprint for future silicon scale, connectivity and organizational-model gaps for the COT operating model, and the need to align business, IT, and superuser stakeholders on a validated To-Be design. The business objective is to establish a reliable baseline, finalize the To-Be blueprint, and support an implementation approach that balances scalability, operational continuity, and cost.

3.2.content:
- Establish end-to-end silicon planning by integrating machine demand with supplier execution across the wafer, die-bank, assembly, and finished-goods lifecycle.
- Transition the silicon supply chain from limited visibility to direct traceability, cost transparency, and a structured audit trail under the Customer Owned Tooling model.
- Enable yield-, capacity-, and scenario-aware planning through Kinaxis and S/4HANA, with planning visibility across TSMC and identified OSAT partners.
- Configure Kinaxis and SAP PP/MM to support silicon manufacturing processes, including supply planning, collaboration, and closed-loop decision-making.
- Implement structured partner collaboration through E2Open and related integrations required for supplier commit-versus-plan visibility and end-to-end work-in-process tracking.
- Deliver the program in three phases over an 18-month term, progressing from foundational lot traceability to expanded analytical and planning capability.
- Drive user adoption through organizational change management, including stakeholder engagement, readiness assessment, communications, training, and adoption tracking across impacted functions.
- Provide a single planning layer for silicon supply decision-making and improve allocation speed, supplier transparency, and reduction of manual reconciliation.

3.3.content:
The target-state process flow will establish Google’s direct COT operating model across foundry and OSAT partners, with SAP S/4HANA as the transaction, traceability, and cost backbone, E2Open as the external collaboration layer, and Kinaxis as the planning platform. The process is expected to start with demand and supply signals in Kinaxis, flow through forecast, commit, and purchase order collaboration with TSMC and OSAT partners through E2Open, and continue into SAP S/4HANA for subcontracting, goods movements, process execution, cost capture, and lot-based traceability from wafer through finished goods.

The target-state flow will cover:
- planning BOM, yield-aware demand, and capacity signals in Kinaxis
- forecast, commit, acknowledgment, and PO message exchange with TSMC and OSAT partners through E2Open
- inventory and subcontracting PO processing for wafers, raw materials, and OSAT conversion services in SAP S/4HANA
- receipt, yield recording, batch/lot traceability, and genealogy across Wafer Lot > Probe > Die Bank > Assembly > Test > Finished Goods
- cost and controlling integration to support the COT cost model and financial visibility
- reporting and analytics for cost, yield, and genealogy outcomes

The detailed to-be flow, including partner onboarding sequence, message design, organizational mapping, and system boundary decisions, will be finalized during the Explore phase. `<CONFIRM: include process-flow diagram if approved source diagram is available for client-facing use>`

4.1.content:
- In scope geographies include Taiwan, Malaysia, and the United States.
- The baseline operational flows cover TSMC supply and wafer-related activities in Taiwan, OSAT processing with named partners including SPIL and KYEC, substrate procurement including UMTC, and export/import movements for Taiwan to USA.
- International logistics and trade-compliance scope includes the Taiwan to USA lane and example international flows such as Taiwan to Penang, Malaysia, phased in line with the agreed rollout.
- Intra-Taiwan OSAT-to-OSAT movements are included where required for execution visibility and stock transfer processes.
- Additional international trade lanes, expanded OSAT partner onboarding, and any WMS/TMS-enabled international flows are included only to the extent confirmed for later phases of the engagement.
- Delivery locations for Bristlecone resources and any on-site presence are `<CONFIRM: delivery location(s) and any required on-site geography>`.

4.2.content:
- End-to-end Customer Owned Tooling (COT) supply chain processes are in scope for Google Silicon across constrained supply planning with yield, material master governance, batch and lot traceability, and commit visibility spanning production planning, quality management, materials management, and controlling activities owned by Google.
- In-scope manufacturing and supply execution processes include wafer demand and wafer starts, foundry purchase order and goods receipt flows, wafer probe, wafer saw and die bank, OSAT subcontracting, assembly, burn-in, unit test, system-level test where applicable, QA, pack and ship, and rack and tray assembly and test.
- In-scope planning and visibility processes include supply, constraint, and inventory planning; weekly commits and WIP visibility by lot and location; handoff visibility from wafer through die, package, and finished goods; and yield-informed planning signals to support the ASIC commit process.
- In-scope quality and test processes include wafer lot information capture, yield recording by lot, in-process inspection at OSAT stages, unit- and lot-level test data handling, fail data analysis, and genealogy-linked quality visibility through the Silicon Data Hub and planning layers.
- In-scope procurement and materials processes include material master definition for wafers and raw materials, bill of materials management, foundry and OSAT vendor and subcontract purchase order structures, supplier master setup for TSMC and OSAT partners, and substrate / component supply commit visibility.
- In-scope finance-related processes include cost modeling, OSAT service charge structure definition, actual costing against WIP events, yield variance posting, and lot-level cost visibility; FICO configuration remains with Google.
- The Explore phase will confirm the current-state baseline and finalize the to-be process blueprint for subcontracting, yield recording, traceability, enterprise structure, master data, transactional scope, and process boundaries between SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, Kinaxis, and the test / analytics hub.
- Out of scope unless expressly added through change control: net-new processes beyond TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL in the approved phases, company-confidential analytics not made available by Google, and `<CONFIRM: any additional business processes Google wants explicitly excluded from this SOW>`.

4.3.content:
- In scope are the technical components required to enable phased manufacturing visibility, business go-live, and expanded supply-chain capabilities across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, Silicon Data Hub, E2Open Vendor Collaboration, SFTP-based data flows, BigQuery reporting, and Amber Road for trade-compliance-related design and configuration.

- SAP S/4HANA scope includes material master setup for wafer, raw materials, and substrate; bill of materials support; TSMC inventory purchase orders and goods receipt; OSAT subcontracting purchase-order structures for SPIL and KYEC; full lot traceability from wafer through die, assembly, and finished goods; 4-step OSAT routing; actual costing runs; yield variance posting; TSMC scheduling agreement and UMTC substrate procurement support; OSAT subcontracting POs; and SAP STOs for intra-Taiwan OSAT-to-OSAT movements.

- Silicon Data Hub scope includes lot genealogy, unit-level test data storage, test-data ingestion from SFTP, and in-process inspection / manufacturing data visibility required to support traceability and yield analysis.

- Kinaxis scope includes wafer demand signaling to TSMC, planning BOM consumption from GPLM / G-Plan, basic wafer supply planning below SoC level, yield-adjusted netting, die-bank inventory buffering, OSAT capacity and constraint planning, automated demand-signal and commit flows, exception feedback handling, and full scenario simulation / multi-sourcing in the expanded phase.

- E2Open scope includes TSMC structured commits, OSAT commit / recommit flows, OSAT WIP event visibility, ASN processing, intra-Taiwan shipment visibility, Quanta ASN and proof-of-delivery visibility for the Taiwan-to-USA leg, and exception-signal feedback to Kinaxis.

- Product test and quality technical scope includes SAP lot information at wafer goods receipt, yield recording per lot, XY die-location fusion at probe, yield summaries to Kinaxis, yield exception signaling, and the AI/Arcus yield-prediction model. AI-enabled outputs, if used in delivery or decision support, remain subject to Google-approved AI governance and review controls.

- Finance-related technical scope includes SAP cost-modeling enablement, OSAT service-charge structure support, lot-level cost visibility, full product-costing support with yield-adjusted margins, and finance analytics in BigQuery / the reporting layer. CO/FICO configuration owned by Google’s internal team is excluded from Bristlecone scope.

- Trade and logistics technical scope includes trade-compliance design, Amber Road integration/configuration for export and import documentation between Taiwan and the United States, and logistics mapping for confirmed in-scope WMS/TMS flows. International WMS/TMS flows are limited to `<CONFIRM: whether international WMS/TMS scope is included in this SOW>`.

4.4.content:
Bristlecone will provide program management, fit-gap analysis, to-be process design, solution design, configuration, build, functional specifications, test planning and execution support for UT, SIT, and UAT, data migration support, cutover planning, deployment support, hypercare, organizational change management, training, and knowledge transfer.

Services will be delivered in a phased Agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy releases for Google Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain processes covering Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, and related integrations required for the approved scope.

Delivery services include implementation of end-to-end silicon planning capabilities to improve supply chain visibility, constrained supply planning, yield-aware planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, and supplier commit versus plan transparency across TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Google Hub, and warehouse operations.

Integration services include retaining Google’s existing integration framework used for machines planning, adapting the current data template for Silicon planning needs, enabling Kinaxis consumption of additional inbound E2Open capacity and contract manufacturer data, and delivering approved delta interfaces between SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and other confirmed systems within scope.

Testing and deployment services include regression and performance testing, release readiness support, go-live support for phased deployments, and post-go-live hypercare for each release.

OCM services include communications, training, readiness checks, and user adoption support aligned to the phased rollout plan.

Any services related to modules, systems, or process areas not expressly identified in this SOW, including unvalidated integrations such as SAP ↔ PLM (Agile), are out of scope unless approved through the Change Management Process.

4.5.content:
Application scope includes Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open for the Google Silicon business unit.

- **Kinaxis:** supply planning, constraint planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, demand and commit visibility, yield-adjusted netting, die bank inventory buffering, OSAT capacity consumption from E2Open, multi-sourcing, allocation, and scenario planning.
- **SAP S/4HANA:** Production Planning (PP) and Materials Management (MM) to support material master and BOM management, wafer and raw-material procurement, vendor and scheduling-agreement setup, PO/GR processing, OSAT subcontracting structures, lot traceability, routing, actual costing inputs, and cost visibility.
- **E2Open:** collaboration and inbound data layer for inventory, capacity, CM, ASN, and partner data exchange across TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL.
- Existing integration and data-template frameworks will be retained where feasible and extended for Silicon planning requirements, including incremental delta interfaces identified during the Explore phase.
- Technical ABAP development, analytics expansion, PI/PO or BTP detail, and any WMS/TMS or expanded international logistics capabilities are limited to the extent confirmed during discovery and subsequent phase planning: `<CONFIRM: final application boundary for ABAP, analytics, PI/PO or BTP, and any WMS/TMS scope>`.

5.content:
The solution architecture will use Kinaxis as the planning layer, SAP S/4HANA as the execution system for Production Planning and Materials Management, and E2Open for supplier collaboration and external execution visibility across TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. The design will support end-to-end visibility across wafer, die, and finished-goods stages, including constrained supply planning, yield-aware planning, inventory planning, analytics, reporting, and batch traceability. Existing data templates will be reused and adjusted for Silicon planning needs.

The deployment model is phased and Agile, progressing through Explore, Build, and Deploy releases. Bristlecone will retain Google’s existing integration framework used for machine planning and extend it through incremental delta interfaces identified during discovery. Kinaxis will be configured to consume additional inbound data from E2Open, including capacity information and CM data for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. Delta integration using SAP BTP is in scope for the SAP S/4HANA landscape.

The architecture assumes BOM explosion is managed through PLM and can be leveraged by the current SAP and Kinaxis landscape, and that Google’s inventory ownership begins after probe completion at TSMC and transfers at goods receipt. For Phases 1 and 2, the operating model is limited to Taiwan plants and hubs, with international mid-stream flows deferred to Phase 3.

Change governance will be managed through a cross-functional delivery structure spanning S/4HANA, Kinaxis, integration, and organizational change management, with oversight from a joint steering committee and program leadership. Architecture, integration, and deployment decisions that affect scope, timeline, or commercials will be routed through formal change control. `<TECH TEAM: insert architecture diagram if available, showing Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, PLM/GPlan, SAP BTP, and supplier touchpoints>`

6.1.content:
Bristlecone will deliver the engagement through a phased Agile methodology structured as Explore, Build, and Deploy, executed in waves across the approved implementation scope. The approach starts with business process design, baseline integration analysis, and scope confirmation before system configuration. Build activities will cover Kinaxis setup, required SAP S/4HANA and E2Open enablement, delta integration development on the retained integration framework, data validation, and test preparation. Deploy activities will include SIT, UAT, go-live readiness, release deployment, and hypercare.

Delivery will run on parallel SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis tracks, with E2Open support where required, to establish Kinaxis as the planning orchestration layer while SAP remains the execution backbone. The methodology includes closed-loop planning enablement across fab and OSAT supply-chain flows, with integration of master and transactional data, supplier collaboration, and engineering collaboration through the Silicon Data Hub and APIs.

The program will be governed through regular weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews to track milestones, risks, dependencies, and decisions across business and IT stakeholders. Change management will be domain-led, with role-based training built from approved process designs and aligned across Google, OSAT, and foundry partners.

The rollout is planned as an MVP in two phases followed by a third scaling phase. Phase 3 will be delivered through fixed-capacity rollout support for additional scope, including future procurement-cycle work and onboarding of new OSAT partners. Where prerequisite business events occur before a planned release, interim manual processes will be used until the relevant solution capability is live.

7.1.content:
Bristlecone will govern the engagement through a phased program structure aligned to the agreed workstreams and release plan, with oversight focused on readiness for Phase 1 Manufacturing Visibility, Phase 2 Business Go-Live and Hypercare, and Phase 3 Expanded Scope. Governance reviews will track delivery progress, cross-workstream dependencies, scope decisions, and risks affecting milestone readiness.

Project governance will operate at three levels:
- Working-level reviews across the delivery workstreams to manage day-to-day execution, dependencies, and issue resolution.
- Program-level reviews to assess phase readiness, milestone status, and cross-functional decisions affecting SAP, Kinaxis, E2Open, Silicon Data Hub, finance, procurement, and quality workstreams.
- Executive escalation reviews for decisions that affect scope, timeline, budget, or business readiness.

Escalation will follow a defined path from workstream leads to program leadership, then to executive sponsors where resolution requires client direction or approval. Matters requiring escalation include milestone risk, unresolved dependency blockers, deferred scope decisions, changes affecting the phased rollout, and assumptions that prove invalid during execution.

Governance forums will give priority to time-bound decisions tied to the delivery plan, including the Phase 1 readiness target before Thanksgiving 2026, the Dec 4 TSMC PO capability deadline, and any scope decisions required before Phase 2 go-live and Phase 3 expansion under COE governance.

Formal governance cadence, named client approvers, and escalation contacts will be confirmed during project mobilization and documented in the project plan and RACI. `<CONFIRM: final governance cadence and named escalation/approval roles on both sides>`

- The engagement covers Google Silicon COT supply-chain implementation for Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open across Phase 1/Phase 2 scope, with Phase 3 reserved for future scaling and partner onboarding.

22.1.content:
16.1 Milestone Deliverables Matrix 
The milestone deliverables matrix shall align major phase outputs, acceptance points, and commercial triggers across Prepare, Explore, Realize, Deploy/Cutover, and Hypercare. The matrix shall cover, at minimum, the approved project plan, governance plan, workshop schedule, business process and design documents, RICEFW list, integration design, test scripts and results, training materials, cutover readiness artifacts, go-live results, hypercare transition outputs, knowledge-transfer sign-off, and project closure deliverables. The final matrix shall be baselined before execution and maintained through the change control process in Section 17. 

16.2 Deferred Scope Decisions 
- Any open design decision affecting process scope, integrations, localization, reporting, or custom objects shall be resolved before build begins. 
- Decisions requiring closure include, at minimum, finance and controlling dependencies, 3-way match interface definition, subcontractor/vendor payment handling, and master data governance ownership. 
- Any deferred decision with schedule, effort, or commercial impact shall be documented, approved, and reflected in the project plan before the affected phase starts. 

16.3 Integration & Custom Code Safeguards 
- Integration scope shall be baselined by named interface and connected system before realization activities begin. 
- Custom development shall be governed through an approved RICEFW list, technical specifications, build prioritization, and formal design review. 
- Additions or changes to integrations, interfaces, reports, forms, workflows, enhancements, conversions, or localization objects after baseline approval shall be handled through Section 17. 
- Mock loads, unit testing, SIT, UAT, cutover readiness, and production support shall be completed against the approved scope baseline. 

16.4 Change Control 
All changes to scope, timeline, deliverables, assumptions, staffing, dependencies, or commercials shall follow the Change Management Process in Section 17. No out-of-scope work shall proceed without documented impact assessment and written approval from authorized project representatives of both parties. 

- Maintain a joint governance cadence with status reporting, risk review, issue tracking, and decision escalation across the project lifecycle. 
- Review risks, assumptions, and dependency status at each phase gate and before go/no-go for production deployment. 
- Confirm the final milestone deliverables matrix and scope baseline before mobilization closes.

22.2.content:
Bristlecone will define phase-specific acceptance criteria for configuration, integrations, data interfaces, and testing outputs before execution of each test cycle. Acceptance will be based on approved test scripts, documented exit criteria, recorded test results, and closure or approved workaround of defects required to support go/no-go decisions.

Quality validation will follow Unit Test, System Integration Test, and User Acceptance Test cycles. Unit Testing will be executed by Bristlecone in the Development environment for configured functionality and interface objects, with results documented and peer reviewed. System Integration Testing will validate end-to-end process execution across integrated systems in the Test/Quality environment with participation from Google core team members and representative business data volumes. User Acceptance Testing will be performed by Google end users in the Test/Quality environment using business-scenario test scripts prepared by Bristlecone to confirm that the solution meets agreed business requirements.

Defects identified during testing will be logged, assigned, resolved, and retested in the designated testing tool. Progression to the next phase or release will require satisfaction of agreed exit criteria and a joint go/no-go decision by the parties’ authorized project leads.

Bristlecone recommends that acceptance criteria remain objective and measurable for each major deliverable and test cycle, including expected process outcomes, interface behavior, data-validation results, and defect-severity thresholds. Any scope growth, additional integrations, or changes to agreed acceptance baselines must be managed through the Change Management Process in Section 17.
